 1                II.   PURPOSE AND SUMMARY OF TESTIMONY AND
 2                                RECOMMENDATIONS

 3   Q.   Why is SPS filing this case?

 4   A.   SPS is at an important juncture in its generation and infrastructure planning. It is

 5        transitioning its generation fleet by retiring and replacing aging units and extending

 6        the operating lives of select cost-effective plants. As part of that transition, SPS

 7        seeks recovery of recently approved investment in new solar and battery projects.

 8        At the same time, SPS is making necessary investments in its information

 9        technology, transmission, and distribution infrastructure—and the people that

10        install and maintain that infrastructure—to support sustained load-growth and to

11        harden the system against increasing security threats, extreme weather, and wildfire

12        risk.

13                SPS is also seeking recovery of previously deferred costs, like increases in

14        excess liability insurance premiums, technology upgrades, and meter replacement

15        costs—costs which reflect an energy landscape that is changing and requiring

16        action by SPS outside of traditional rate case cycles. Additionally, SPS is updating

17        its capital structure to reflect current financial conditions and help maintain a strong

18        credit profile so that it can continue to provide reliable power to New Mexico’s

19        growing economy.


                                                 5

 1               Finally, SPS’s Application addresses the jurisdictional and customer-class

 2        allocation changes driven by New Mexico’s increasing share of SPS’s retail load,

 3        driven in large part by Southeast New Mexico’s growing economy. Aligning New

 4        Mexico’s share of system costs and benefits with its actual usage ensures fair, cost-

 5        based rates across customer classes.

 6               Taken together, these drivers demonstrate SPS’s proactive approach to

 7        delivering safe, cost-effective, and reliable service today in a manner that fairly and

 8        transparently allocates costs, while supporting economic growth, system resilience,

 9        and new business tomorrow. SPS is honored to serve our customers and to support

10        the economic growth in the state by working to keep the electricity flowing and by

11        keeping bills as low as possible.

12   Q.   How does this filing support New Mexico’s energy policy goals?

13   A.   This filing supports New Mexico’s energy policy goals by enabling timely recovery

14        of the investments SPS must make to modernize the grid and maintain safe, reliable,

15        sustainable, and cost-effective electric service in the face of a changing energy

16        landscape. Timely, reliable, and resilient electric service is a cornerstone of

17        economic development. Businesses—particularly in energy-intensive sectors like

18        those SPS serves—depend on uninterrupted power to operate efficiently and plan

19        long-term investments. A dependable grid reduces operational risk, lowers outage-

 7   selected through competitive all-source requests for proposals that sought firm,

 8   accredited capacity for SPS to meet its reliability requirements and replace aging

12   replacement needs and acquisition processes through integrated resource planning

13   and other associated regulatory proceedings facilitates this energy transition.

15   system resilience, including grid reliability, reducing outage risks, protecting

16   against weather-related economic loss, and enabling the clean energy transition.
